The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed to load for many shoppers
Why, in plain words: An administrator switched off a feature setting, which sent account pages through a monthly spending summary that likely breaks, by dividing by zero, for any shopper who has bought before but nothing this month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 39.0% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 4,714.52 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #569 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed to load for many shoppers while legacy-checkout-fallback was off
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 09:27 to 09:35 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 09:38:31 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 09:34:02 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 09:27 UTC and was back to normal at 09:35 UTC, 8 minutes later. 26.3% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 39.0% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 4,714.52 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. An administrator switched off a feature setting, which sent account pages through a monthly spending summary that likely breaks, by dividing by zero, for any shopper who has bought before but nothing this month. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #569, for a person to review and merge. If legacy-checkout-fallback is switched off again, account pages can fail again for shoppers who have past purchases but none this month.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
39.0% - peak error rate
2,526 - requests failed
1.0% to 26.3% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
4,714.52 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With legacy-checkout-fallback off, account pages take the monthly spend-summary path. There, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`, and nothing guards against that number being zero. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError, which `render_spend_summary` passes up to `serve_account_page`, and the page is recorded as failed. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the account page error rate rose far above its usual level.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 16 occurrences in 8 minutes, 09:27–09:34
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 37 occurrences in 38 minutes, 08:57–09:34; # was 0.50% to 39.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 09:31
why 1 The account page requests failed because rendering them raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors first appear in the onset minute.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 The division by zero began when admin switched the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off at 09:27:52 UTC. Before that, every evaluation read the flag as on and account pages rendered normally. Evaluations started reading off in the minute of the change and read off in every minute after it.
  Evidence:
    P1 09:27:52 UTC flag toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
    G153f INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=on - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 08:57–09:26
    Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 09:22
    G7ad6 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 20 / on 180 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 09:27
    G7037 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 7 occurrences in 7 minutes, 09:28–09:34
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 09:28; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change.
      T7
      T8
    Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed 1 flag change by anyone but Argus in the 1 hour before 09:34:11 UTC, and that change was this one.
      T14 09:34:11 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 09:34:11
      P1
why 3 With the flag off, account pages likely take the monthly spend-summary path, which divides by the number of items bought this month, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- The flag change reached all of io-shop's traffic within the minute it was made. No staged rollout and no check before the change was seen. (AI-3)
- No test was seen that runs the account page with legacy-checkout-fallback off for a shopper who has past purchases but none this month. Code-Fix's new tests for that case raise against the current code. (AI-4)
- The HighErrorRate rule waits 5 minutes with its condition holding before it fires, so the error rate stayed high for some time before anything acted on it. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched from on to off at 09:27:52 UTC. Account page requests then began failing with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate rose from about 1% to about 33%. No deployment was involved. | 0.90 | confirmed

Trigger
legacy-checkout-fallback flag went from ON to OFF at 09:27:52 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 09:34:12 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 09:36:58 | Proposed a fix: PR #569 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 09:27 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 09:34 UTC, 7 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #569 | open
AI-3 | Roll out io-shop feature flag changes to a small share of traffic first, and roll them back automatically if the error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Run io-shop's test suite in CI with each feature flag in both states, so a code path a flag opens is tested before the flag can be changed. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Review whether the HighErrorRate rule on io-shop can fire with a shorter hold without becoming noisy. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Lock legacy-checkout-fallback ON against further changes until the fix in PR #569 is merged. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came 6 minutes after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
- 3 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus called in the Investigator Agent.
- 11 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 12 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C1, moved from OFF to ON.
- 2 minutes 8 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 2 minutes 58 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #569.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was brought in to respond.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 12 09:27 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began
 | 09:34 | DETECTED | HighErrorRate on io-shop fired
T1 | 09:34:02 |  | Argus Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
T2 | 09:34:03 |  | Argus Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
T3 | 09:34:04 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 09:34
T4 | 09:34:04 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 361 minutes of metrics
T5 | 09:34:04 |  | Investigator Agent Placed the start of the incident at 09:27
T6 | 09:34:04 |  | Investigator Agent Recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
T7 | 09:34:07 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 09:28
T8 | 09:34:07 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 1 production change
T9 | 09:34:07 |  | Investigator Agent Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
T10 | 09:34:07 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 37 minutes before 09:34
T11 | 09:34:07 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 142 log lines
T12 | 09:34:11 |  | Investigator Agent Formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1
T13 | 09:34:11 |  | Investigator Agent Read every channel available
T14 | 09:34:11 |  | Argus Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 09:34:11
T15 | 09:34:11 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
T16 | 09:34:12 | MITIGATION APPLIED | Mitigation Agent Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C1, moved from OFF to ON
T17 | 09:34:13 |  | Mitigation Agent Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 09:35 - up to 167s
 | 09:35 | IMPACT ENDS | the service was back to normal
T18 | 09:36:08 |  | Mitigation Agent Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 09:34
T19 | 09:36:08 |  | Mitigation Agent Judged the action CONFIRMED
T20 | 09:36:08 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag legacy-checkout-fallback ON and the rule that fired stopped firing
T21 | 09:36:58 |  | Code-Fix Agent Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #569

Response effort
none - engineer time
136,597 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/4a848a74-7d34-4ab0-8689-6d672e93a1f6
The fix it proposed: PR #569 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/569) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 09:27:52 UTC flag toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G153f | INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=on - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 08:57–09:26
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 50 occurrences in 30 minutes, 08:57–09:26
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 37 occurrences in 38 minutes, 08:57–09:34; # was 0.50% to 39.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 09:31
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 09:22
G7ad6 | INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 20 / on 180 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 09:27
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 16 occurrences in 8 minutes, 09:27–09:34
G7037 | INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 7 occurrences in 7 minutes, 09:28–09:34
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py worked out account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month). bought_this_month holds only the purchases marked in_current_month, so it is empty for any shopper who has bought before but not this month. That is an ordinary shopper, not an edge case: the test file's own builder an_account_with_no_purchases_this_month calls it "the ordinary case". For every such account the function raised ZeroDivisionError at line 47. render_spend_summary lets that reach serve_account_page, which records it as a failed page. So any request sent down the monthly path (use_monthly_summary=True) failed for these shoppers. This is the path the flag change opened up.

The fix: when nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0. That is the correct average spend this month for a shopper who spent nothing (their total_this_month_cents is 0). Nothing else changes. The lifetime average and the typical-spend path are untouched. A real failure still propagates as before: an account with no purchases at all still raises from average_spend_per_item, and the existing test that checks this is kept.

The new tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py are written to show two things. First, the monthly average is 0 for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. Second, render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) returns 0 for that shopper rather than raising. Both cases raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code. That makes the page safe with the flag in either state.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-11
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, account pages on io-shop failed to load for some shoppers. An administrator switched off a feature setting, which sent account pages through a monthly spending summary that likely breaks, by dividing by zero, for any shopper who has bought before but nothing this month. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. No on-call responder was paged, so no one was called in to respond. Argus ended the incident by reverting the feature setting (legacy-checkout-fallback), and that reversal is confirmed and still in place. Argus has also proposed a fix, which is open as a draft and has not yet been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
